about:
Low Energy is a COVID era collaboration with Denver based progressive trance producer, Black Wands.

I was really into the Weeknd album, After Hours. I had just bought my first synthesizer to celebrate starting a new job, and I was hungry to explore what it could do.

Stuck inside the house, I was feeling restless, and things were just off between me and my partner. We felt the weight of the world on our relationship, and being stuck inside only amplified that. This song became an outlet for all of that restless energy; A vicarious dance party; A way to break the confinement.

I'd get on a zoom call with Alex (Black Wands), and we'd work on the song for hours. I'd record bits, and send them over, he'd send back his edits. Eventually we got in the same room together, and that's when the song really came to life. He had this tiny keyboard in his home studio. It didn't have enough notes on it to play the melody I had, so I had to take the last note and flip it up an octave, like wrapping the song around the edge of the instrument. And it sounded dope! We tried to "fix" it, but all the feeling went out of it. So we just kept that first take (3:36)

I had never really worked on dance music before, and he had never really done pop. This collaboration brought us both out of our comfort zones, and created a really a unique track.
